F1

B
In a request asking synthesis to wait
A request does not implement synchronization.
In the orchestrator, by joining both tasks before synthesis
A join enforces that both dependencies are available.
By increasing the synthesis output limit
Output capacity does not enforce execution order.
By running synthesis before either analysis
Its required inputs would be missing.
F1
An agent has a fixed monetary budget for external calls. Which TWO controls directly keep execution within that budget?
A
D
Track incurred cost in the execution harness
Measured cumulative cost is needed to decide whether more work is affordable.
Ask the agent to describe itself as economical
A description is not an enforced budget.
Remove cost records after every call
This prevents cumulative enforcement.
Reject further calls when the allowed budget is exhausted

F1

C
Restart every branch regardless of its state
This discards completed work.

Retry the failed branch and retain the completed branch's result

That checks too late.
Only a second unconstrained model

F1

D
Invent an identifier
This risks acting on another account.
Retry lookup with the same missing parameter forever
No new information is obtained.
Mark the ticket resolved
The required work is unfinished.
Enter a waiting-for-input state and resume when valid input arrives
An explicit wait handles a missing prerequisite without fabrication.
F1

Averaging does not resolve factual contradictions.

F1

C
Assume the file will appear

Skip validation because the plan is fluent

Validate dependencies and revise the plan or request the missing input
This addresses the concrete prerequisite.
Increase the number of parallel workers
More workers cannot create an undefined dependency.
F1

A
A structured result with explicit required fields and completion criteria
Required evidence and completion conditions can be validated.
A free-form statement saying the work looks finished
This lacks measurable completion conditions.
The worker's response length
Length does not measure completeness.
The worker's display name
Names do not establish task success.
F1

D
A request for a longer final answer
This does not stop unnecessary work.
A new task for each worker
This increases work after cancellation.
Only a change to the window title
Presentation does not affect execution.
Cancellation to running branches and a terminal cancelled state
Execution state must reflect cancellation and stop further scheduling.
F1

B
Always choose the first specialist
That assigns unsupported work arbitrarily.
Use an explicit fallback that asks for clarification or reports unsupported scope
A defined fallback makes the uncovered case visible.
Discard the request silently
That hides failure from the user.
Send it to every specialist until one sounds confident
Confidence does not establish supported scope and this wastes work.
F2

C
That the ID contains only digits
Syntactic validation does not prove access rights.
That the model says the customer is authorized
The model cannot grant access.
That the authenticated caller is authorized for that tenant and record
Authorization must bind identity to the requested resource.
That the response is valid JSON
Output shape is unrelated to record access.
F2

A
A server-enforced idempotency key tied to the logical operation
Repeated requests can resolve to the same operation rather than duplicate effects.
A different random payment reference on every retry
Different references can create independent payments.
A longer tool description with no server changes
Documentation alone cannot deduplicate effects.
Suppress all timeout errors
Hiding errors does not resolve uncertain completion.
F2

D
Discovery authorizes every tool automatically
Availability is not authorization.
A tool name grants access to all credentials
Names do not define credential scope.
A discovered schema replaces server-side checks
A schema does not enforce caller permissions.
Discovery describes the capability; the application and server must still apply policy
Capability metadata and authorization are separate responsibilities.
F2

B
Return the entire database on every call

Return only the total count and no way to fetch results
The task still needs actual evidence.

The agent cannot know whether relevant data was omitted.

A structured retryable error with the waiting hint and a bounded retry policy
The caller can distinguish throttling and recover within limits.

Invented data is not a recovery strategy.
